messages.content:
Risk: Governance failures
Description: The AI system may outpace regulatory frameworks and oversight mechanisms, potentially leading to ineffective governance and the inability to manage AI risks appropriately.
Concern: None
Policy: Medical Professional Impersonation

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0033071: Impaired task monitoring — Impaired ability to keep track of one's problem-solving success or failure, and to identify and correct mistakes during performance of a goal. [found by 3/9 queries]
  Siblings: Impaired ability to plan, Impaired self monitoring, Impaired ability to organize
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_0007344: executive dysfunction AE — This is an AE which is a disruption to the efficacy of the executive functions, which is a group of cognitive processes that regulate, control, and manage other cognitive processes. [found by 3/9 queries]
  Siblings: suicide attempt AE, obsessive thoughts AE, distractibility AE
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/RegulatoryAgencies/RegulatoryReport: regulatory report — document required to support operational transparency that demonstrates compliance with some specification, law, policy, restriction, or other rule specified by a regulatory agency [found by 7/9 queries]
  Siblings: technical specification document, registry, transaction record
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#DangerousInformation: Dangerous Information — Knowledge or instructions that enable serious physical harm, weapons production, or dangerous activities when acquired or executed by untrained individuals outside regulated contexts. [found by 7/9 queries]
  Siblings: Sexual Content, Intellectual Property, Hate and Discrimination
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/SitesAndFacilities/Facility: facility — something established to serve a particular purpose, make some course of action or operation easier, or provide some capability or service [found by 7/9 queries]

axes.rationale: Governance failures often stem from a lack of or inadequate regulatory frameworks. Regulatory reports are documents that demonstrate compliance with these frameworks, making them relevant to the risk.

AI systems can generate or process dangerous information that may outpace existing regulations. This risk is particularly relevant in the context of medical professional impersonation, where AI-generated information could have significant health consequences.
